label: Late original-phase o/q/e/l/g/3/v/b/m/w/x input in a sequence that began with a y/digit/d/r/j/p-type token
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (95% of mass), never at t=0-1 and rarely at t=2. Within that phase it is active at orig_idx>=3, with rate rising to about 20% at orig_idx 5-8. It is driven by the current input being one of a specific token group (o, q, e, l, g, 3, v, b, m, and more weakly w and x; o and q have the highest rates, around 17%), mostly on the first occurrence of that token. It is gated by sequence context: activation depends strongly on the earlier tokens, best captured by the first token being from a complementary group (y, digits 0-2, d, r, j, p, c, u, ...). The same trigger tokens after a prefix starting with m/b/a/v/l/z-like letters are mostly silent. Top activations (o, q, e, g at steps 5-7 after prefixes like y y 0 r i, j 2 c r d f f) chain across several consecutive trigger tokens. Weaker firing occurs at <DEL> (about 5% of mass, usually when the preceding inputs were trigger tokens). It is essentially silent in the copy phase. Imperfect: the prefix dependence looks like graded evidence accumulated over all earlier tokens rather than a clean first-token rule, so precision and recall are both around 0.65-0.75.
